suggestions.title: The commits check catches a mislabelled compare only when it is older, not when it is a descendant; the comment says it covers branch-name reads in general
suggestions.evidence: The guard at lines 308-311 is `compare.headSha !== pr.headSha || !compare.commits.includes(pr.headSha)`. The GateInputs comment at lines 101-103 says the commits clause is there for a compare read by branch name or from cache that the shell still labels with pr.headSha ("这一条出自响应本身，不只信外壳填的值"). That only holds when the compare is older than the head. For a descendant, base..NEWER contains HEAD, so `includes` passes. The tsx probe confirmed it: compare {headSha: HEAD, commits: [EARLIER, HEAD, NEWER], files of NEWER}, with verdicts bound to NEWER's digest, returns {ready: true, headSha: HEAD, patchDigest: digest(NEWER)}. This is the run-4 finding again, now guarded only by the shell's label. There is no caller yet, and the documented contract (request the compare by SHA) prevents it, so this is not blocking.
suggestions.failurePath: An S4 shell reads the PR at HEAD. The author then pushes NEWER. The shell fetches compare by branch name, or from a response cached under the branch, and fills in headSha = pr.headSha. Its commits include HEAD, so the guard passes. mergeReadiness binds NEWER's patch digest, and the verdicts on it, to HEAD and can return ready. Suggestion: either correct the comment so it says only the older direction is caught from the response, or make the guard derive the descendant case from the response too. For example, pass commits with their parents and treat the compare as not read at the head when any listed commit has pr.headSha as a parent.

suggestions.title: Checks head binding trusts only the shell's label; no response-derived backstop like the compare's commits check, so acceptance item 1 holds for checks only when the shell is honest
suggestions.evidence: For compare, the guard at line 311 requires both compare.headSha === pr.headSha and compare.commits.includes(pr.headSha) (code-review finding 1 restored the response-derived half, pinned by the 'compare 自报读在 PR 的 head 上' test). For checks, line 215 compares only checks.headSha, and GateCheckRun/GateCommitStatus (lines 41-52) carry no head_sha/sha. Code-review finding 2 was left to S4 as a contract comment, and no test can pin it at this layer.
suggestions.failurePath: An S4 shell lists check-runs by branch ref or from a cached response and fills checks.headSha = pr.headSha. The runs belong to the previous push and are green while the real head's CI is pending or failed. mergeReadiness reports no required-check-pending or required-check-failed. No caller exists yet, so this is not reachable at this head. Carrying per-run head_sha and the combined-status sha in the input would let readiness verify the binding and let a test pin it, the same way the compare side is pinned.

suggestions.title: Malformed headSha (uppercase/short) becomes an endless transient wait; the failure mode is deferred to S4 with no test or enforcement at the pure layer
suggestions.evidence: Strict equality at lines 215 and 311. The doc comment (lines 108-109) says the shell must pass 'malformed' for a non-40-hex compare headSha so that it does not 'become a forever-unmatched wait', but readiness itself does not check the format. checks has no malformed state at all (Risk section, code-review finding 3).
suggestions.failurePath: The shell passes compare.headSha or checks.headSha as an uppercase or 7-char SHA. Every patrol gives transient patch-unavailable or required-checks-unreadable, and the gate never escalates to human. A /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/ check in readiness mapping to compare-malformed (human), plus a test, would make the documented fail-closed behaviour enforced and pinned instead of a contract note.

suggestions.title: PR body states the malformed-SHA contract more loosely than the code comment
suggestions.failurePath: The PR body says the shell must 'pass a SHA that is not 40 hex characters as malformed'. The contract written at the input type says 'headSha 不是 40 位小写 SHA 时外壳同样传 malformed', which also requires lowercase. Under the body's wording, a 40-character uppercase SHA would be passed through. readiness.ts then compares it with strict equality (`compare.headSha !== pr.headSha`), which gives the transient patch-unavailable on every patrol: the endless wait that code-review finding 3 describes. The code comment is the authoritative one, but S4 may be built from the PR description.
suggestions.evidence: PR body What section: 'pass a SHA that is not 40 hex characters as `'malformed'`'; readiness.ts:108 '40 位小写 SHA'; s2-r9-reviews.txt finding 3 (uppercase or short SHA leads to an endless transient wait).
